biological_reference.closest_mechanism: VTA/LC dopaminergic modulation of hippocampal place-field density/reorganisation at reward locations
dependencies: expectation-dependent DA reward-proximity ramp (Krishnan et al. 2022)
biological_reference.divergence: Mixed but load-bearing lit corpus already exists in targeted_review_sd_024 (5 entries): Retailleau & Morris 2018 (supports/0.75), Krishnan et al. 2022 (supports/0.82, DA ramp is expectation/proximity-dependent -- and its summary explicitly says this SUPPORTS the SD-012 benefit*drive scaling, it does NOT predict magnitude-insensitivity), Xiao et al. 2020 (mixed/0.58), Duvelle et al. 2019 (weakens/0.70, NO modulation of place-cell activity by goal VALUE -- and its summary explicitly states that if REE's density scales cleanly with benefit_magnitude, 'that is a divergence from the biology, not a convergence with it'; the substrate's dopamine_signal=benefit_magnitude*drive_level formula commits to exactly that linear scaling), Shao et al. 2025 (mixed/0.55, a gain-only alternative mechanism C2 is meant to rule out). CORRECTION after adversarial review: an earlier draft of this autopsy claimed the flat benefit_magnitude split was 'a confirmed prediction' from Krishnan+Duvelle. That is wrong and is corrected here: this run has essentially zero benefit_magnitude variance (CV ~1.6%), so it cannot confirm OR refute either paper's prediction on the magnitude axis -- it is uninformative on that axis, not confirmatory. Duvelle's prediction is actually the opposite of what the substrate's linear formula implies, and remains untested (not confirmed) by this run.

targets.recommended_evidence_quality_note: 2026-09-14 failure-autopsy (V3-EXQ-900, resolving GFLAG-0246; adversarially red-teamed on a different model, verdict CONTESTED -> corrected below). (1) FLAT BENEFIT_MAGNITUDE FINDING: mean_benefit_magnitude_across_cluster_sizes_ge2 (0.5577) vs cluster_size_1 (0.5582) is NOT a functional discriminator and does not falsify or qualify anything. benefit_magnitude is the near-constant environmental input (CV ~1.6% across all 57 pooled events) multiplied by the genuinely variable drive_level (34x range) to form dopamine_signal; a magnitude-keyed split was never going to show a gap by construction. This finding is CONFIRMED by independent recompute and does not need further work. (2) THE DEEPER, VALIDATED CONCERN: GFLAG-0246's underlying worry -- that nothing in the combination rule (C1 AND C2 AND C4) actually tests the FUNCTIONAL half of the claim's label -- is SUBSTANTIALLY CORRECT, though not via the benefit_magnitude route. Traced to source: the manifest's own field 'C2_cluster_size_vs_density' (measured rho=0.5166) is NOT computed on raw density (the signal field.py's own docstring identifies as 'the signal the SD-025 curiosity drive follows') -- it is computed on density_delta (post-event minus pre-event density AT the event's own location). Recomputed directly from per_seed_rows: rho(cluster_size, RAW density) = 0.1775, below the driver's own pre-registered RHO_LIVE_MIN=0.30 bar (driver docstring lines 97-100, 155-157 name 'density', not 'density_delta'; the substitution is made in evaluate(), documented in code comments as a fix for a field-history confound found in a pre-run probe -- but the docstring's formal PRE-REGISTERED ACCEPTANCE section was never updated to match). Further: density_delta is substantially an ARITHMETIC function of cluster_size and the fixed jitter/bandwidth geometry (single-center delta = 1.0 +/- 2e-6 for 51/51 events; per-center delta for clusters ~0.49, matching exp(-E[||jitter||^2]/(2*bw^2)) exactly) -- it is closer to a re-run of the P0 synthetic sweep (R2, rho=1.0) than a live functional-propagation test, and at the smallest cluster size (n=2) one of two observed events reads LOWER density at the contact point than a single center would (delta 0.958 < 1.000), directly undermining 'more centers -> more density read here' as a live-tested proposition. VERDICT: the PASS is a genuine, well-powered, LOO-robust (min 0.495 on C1) confirmation of the REPRESENTATIONAL sub-clause (C1: DA responds to live cluster allocation) and the MECH-233 ASYMMETRY (C4: 0 of 1403 harm calls allocate a cluster) -- both robust and claim-confidence-bearing. It does NOT establish that this structural difference propagates into the STANDING density signal the rest of the substrate (SD-025's curiosity drive) actually reads; the properly-operationalized version of that test fails on this run's own live data. Recorded as narrow_supports: true. SD-024 stays candidate (status unchanged); the claims.yaml CONFIRMING(mechanism) section's C2 entry ('measured 0.517') should be corrected to note it is the delta-based figure and that the raw-density form (0.18) does not clear the pre-registered bar. This also completes, for this one instance, the 'may invalidate the run's VERDICT, not merely its recording' governance question GFLAG-0249 deferred to a future decision -- resolved here as: does not invalidate the PASS's representational/asymmetry evidence, does invalidate the label's functional half and claims.yaml's current C2 characterization. RECOMMENDED FUTURE WORK (not queued from this autopsy; governance chips once ratified): a redesign that operationalizes functional propagation via a STANDING read (e.g. density at a fixed post-event delay/revisit, or an explicit baseline-subtracted trend across an episode) rather than an immediate event-marginal delta, and that additionally sweeps benefit_magnitude at pinned drive_level (the axis Duvelle 2019 and the substrate's own linear formula make opposite, currently-untested predictions on) alongside the already-planned drive_level sweep.

learning_extracted: GFLAG-0246's core concern -- nothing in the combination rule tests the claim's functional half -- is SUBSTANTIALLY CORRECT, though the flag's own cited evidence (the flat benefit_magnitude split) was the wrong route to it. The real route: the manifest's recorded C2 statistic is computed on density_delta, not the pre-registered raw density; the raw-density form measures 0.1775, below the 0.30 bar, on this run's own live sample.

density_delta for this design is substantially an arithmetic function of cluster_size and fixed RBF jitter/bandwidth geometry (single-center delta = 1.0 to 6 decimal places for 51/51 events; per-center cluster delta ~0.49, matching the jitter-kernel expectation exactly) -- it is close to a re-run of the P0 synthetic sweep (R2) with live jitter, not an independent live-functional-propagation test.

The flat mean_benefit_magnitude comparison is confirmed uninformative (near-constant input, CV ~1.6%), but it is NOT 'a confirmed prediction' from the cited literature as an earlier draft of this autopsy asserted -- Krishnan 2022 says nothing about magnitude-insensitivity, and Duvelle 2019's prediction is the OPPOSITE of the substrate's linear benefit_magnitude*drive_level formula. The run is simply uninformative on that axis, in either direction. This correction was caught by an adversarial red-team pass on a different model and independently verified before landing.

At the smallest observed cluster size (n=2), one of two live events reads a LOWER density at the contact point than a single center would have (density_delta 0.958 vs the single-center baseline of 1.000) -- a real geometry effect from jitter dispersion at this bandwidth, worth recording for any future redesign of the density read.

Sample-size caveat: R3's pooled-expansion-event floor (5) was cleared by exactly 1 event; the C1 correlation is leave-one-out robust (drops to 0.495 minimum on removing any single expansion event) so the PASS does not hinge on one event, but the design's overall precision would benefit from a larger budget before being leaned on heavily by SD-025/ARC-057 downstream work.
